# dsh-deepseek-webchat-claude-skin

The Claude look for the DeepSeek panel: a dark and light skin for the DeepSeek
page that
`@jaychang1

989/dsh-webchat` embeds
in a `<webview>`, plus the sidebar rename that carries the rebrand to the pa

ebchat` embeds
in a `<webview>`, plus the sidebar rename that carries the rebrand to the panel
edge.

One profile, two jobs: webchat keeps owning the embed and its updates, this
package owns the paint.

It does not vendor, patch or re-export webchat, so the
two release independently.
At a glance:

- **What changes**: two colour palettes, the brand artwork, the code-block
surfaces, the "thinking"

fade, and one host-side label.
- **How**: a single CSS text handed to the webview's own `insertCSS`,

plus one
text-node rename in the DSH document. Nothing else crosses a boundary.
- **What it cannot

do**: touch the guest DOM, the network, cookies, storage, the
user agent or the login flow, or run s

cript in the guest.
- **Dependencies**: none. Six files, no install scripts, one readable generated

bundle.
- **Evidence**: 42 code-level tests and a real-Chromium mount check, both behind
`npm run ve

.
- **Evidence**: 42 code-level tests and a real-Chromium mount check, both behind
`npm run verify`.
## What changed recently
**0.3.3 — README only**

No code change. The release notes below were rewritten for someone installing
the plugin rather than

someone reading the fix, and the install command at the
top no longer points at an old version.
**0.3.2 — the sidebar now says "Chat"**

The row used to stay "Chat DeepSeek" no matter what you did. The plugin watched
one node, but the si

debar row turns up six levels below it, and the old code only
looked two levels down. The first swee

p at startup missed it too, because the
sidebar has not been drawn yet at that point. So both attemp

ts came up empty and
the label never changed.

It now searches the whole subtree with no depth limit and repeats that on every
change, so the row s

tays renamed across re-renders, collapses and tooltip
rebuilds. There is a regression test that puts
the row five wrappers deep.
**0.3.1 — the sidebar row renames, and a light theme**

Adds the light palette and the Claude wordmark on the DeepSeek page, and fixes
the sidebar row going

back to "Chat DeepSeek" after the panel re-rendered: React
reuses the existing text node when only

the label changes, so the observer never
saw those updates and the rename was applied once at mount

and then quietly
overwritten. The observer now also watches character data. (0.3.2 found a second,
d
eeper cause for the same symptom — see above.)
**0.3.0 — first release**

Dark and light Claude palettes for the DeepSeek page, the brand artwork, and the
code-block surfaces

ark and light Claude palettes for the DeepSeek page, the brand artwork, and the
code-block surfaces.
## What it changes

This is the complete list. Everything is a stylesheet rule in the guest, except
the last row, which

mplete list. Everything is a stylesheet rule in the guest, except
the last row, which is DSH chrome.
| Where | Surface | Change | Anchored on |
| guest | design tokens | 98 custom properties per theme: 30 static scale stops, 67 semantic aliases

, the "thinking" gradient | `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` / `body:not([data-ds-dark-theme])` |
| guest
| brand artwork | the 143x23 lockup and the two marks (27x24, 35x26) replaced by the Claude lockup a

nd starburst, inlined as data URIs | the `viewBox` attribute |
| guest | code blocks | per-theme sur
face, text and selection colours; the dark toolbar button recoloured | `.md-code-block-dark` / `.md-

code-block-light` |
| host | sidebar row | "Chat DeepSeek" → "Chat", in the label's text node and it
s `aria-label` | the exact label string |

**Tokens.** The 30 static stops remap the site's neutral ramps to a warm
Claude-neutral ramp and its

accent family to terracotta. The 67 aliases cover
canvas and surface layers, the four label levels,

borders, the brand family,
button fills, interaction tints, markdown surfaces, sidebar, bubbles, co

mposer,
scrollbars, toast and tooltip. Every declaration is `!important`, because the
site sets the
same names from its own variable block and would otherwise win.

The site has exactly two theme states and marks them by toggling
`data-ds-dark-theme` on `<body>`; t

here is no light attribute and no
`prefers-color-scheme` signal. So there are two palettes, scoped t

o that
attribute and its absence, and only one can ever match. Switching themes is a
cascade change:
no observer, no re-injection.

**Palette.** Dark is Claude's near-black canvas (`#191919`, layers at `#212121`).
Light is Claude's

paper ramp (`#faf9f5` canvas, warm ink text) with the same
terracotta accent (`#d97757`). Light text

tokens are chosen to clear WCAG AA on
the light surfaces; the accent *text* stop is darker than the

fill stop, exactly
as the site itself does it. White on the accent fill measures 3.12:1 — that is a
UI component, not body text, and the one deliberate sub-AA pairing in the skin.
[该节后续省略]
## What it never does

- No DOM edits in the guest. No node is added, removed, moved or restyled inline.
The only guest wri

te is a stylesheet.
- No network. No `fetch`, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource or beacon; no remote URL i

n
the sheet (SVG data URIs only); no fonts, no images.
- No cookie, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`

or `indexedDB` access; no
`navigator.userAgent` read or override.
- No script execution in the gues

t, no `executeJavaScript`, no text or input
injection, no navigation (`window.open`, `location.href/

assign/replace`).
- No login-state automation. It never reads, drives or clears a session, and no
se

lector targets a login, captcha, challenge, verification, dialog, toast,
alert, error, warning or fo

rm surface.
- No hiding, moving or disabling site UI. The allowed properties are
`background*`, `col

or`, `visibility` and custom properties — no `position`,
`z-index`, `pointer-events`, `display` or `
tyle or handler is touched.

That restraint is not decoration. The DeepSeek page decides whether a client
looks like a supported

browser, and webchat already negotiates that boundary
carefully. A skin has no business joining that

ebchat already negotiates that boundary
carefully. A skin has no business joining that conversation.
